ex: 시험공부를 **하느라고** 잠을 못 잤어요. — Because I was studying for the exam, I couldn't sleep.

im-02-03-02.h: Present Stem (-는 바람에) vs Past Tense Error (✕ -았/었는 바람에)

a.d: Always attaches to the basic present verb stem, even when the entire event happened in the past.
ex: 바람이 세게 **부는 바람에** 우산이 뒤집혔어요. — Because the wind blew hard, the umbrella turned inside out.

b.d: Never insert past tense markers like -았/었- before -는 바람에 (e.g., 불었는 바람에 ✕, 쏟았는 바람에 ✕).
ex: 우유를 쏟**는 바람에** 식탁을 닦았어요. (O) / 쏟았는 바람에 (X)

im-02-03-02.tip: Keep the connector in the present: [verb stem] + -는 바람에, with past tense placed on the final verb.

im-02-03-02.hint: 불다 drops ㄹ and takes -는 바람에 directly without past tense: 부는 바람에.
im-02-03-02.why: Past tense cannot precede -는 바람에, and the ㄹ-batchim stem drops ㄹ: 부는 바람에.

im-02-03-04.h: Polite Explanation of Unavoidable Circumstances vs Blaming Others

a.d: Used in apologies to convey that an unintended mishap happened beyond one's foresight, paired with polite apologies.
ex: 신호등이 고장 나**는 바람에** 길이 막혀 늦었습니다. 죄송합니다. — I apologize that I was late because traffic lights broke down.

b.d: If constantly repeated without taking responsibility, it sounds like shifting blame entirely to external forces.
ex: 동생이 늦게 깨우**는 바람에** 늦었어요! (Sounds irresponsible)

im-02-03-04.tip: When using -는 바람에 at work, always follow up with an apology or alternative solution.
